2014–2019 | team5 = [[Jeonju KCC Egis]] | highlights = * [[Korean Basketball League|KBL]] championship (2009, 2011) * [[KBL Playoffs Most Valuable Player Award|KBL Playoffs MVP]] (2011) * 2× KBL All-Star (2010, 2011) * 3× [[KBL Best 5]] (2010, 2011, 2016) * [[KBL Rookie of the Year Award|KBL Rookie of the Year]] (2009) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{KOR}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Asian Games]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2010 Asian Games|2010 Guangzhou]]|[[Basketball at the 2010 Asian Games|Men's basketball]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Asia Championship]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2011 FIBA Asia Championship|2011 Wuhan]]|[[2011 FIBA Asia Championship|Men's basketball]]}} }} {{Infobox Korean name/auto |hangul=%하승진 |hanja=河昇鎮 }} '''Ha Seung-jin''' ({{Korean|hangul=하승진}}; born August 4, 1985) is a South Korean former professional [[basketball]] player who has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. He was a second round draft pick (46th overall) of the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. At 7 ft 3 in, 305 lb, he was among the tallest players in the NBA. He is also the first and only [[South Koreans|South Korean]] to have played in the NBA. ==Early life and college career== Ha Seung-jin attended his father's alma mater [[:ko:삼일상업고등학교|Samil Commercial High School]] in [[Suwon]] with his childhood friend [[Yang Hee-jong]], who was a year older. The duo led Samil's basketball team to its first ever national championship title. He initially planned on entering the [[2003 NBA draft]] held in June but decided on playing college basketball first and accepted an early offer from [[Yonsei University]].{{cite news|title=하승진 "연대냐 고대냐"… 28일 진로 대학 결정|url=https://www.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2003/04/27/2003042770185.html|work=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]|date=27 April 2003|language=ko}} It meant that he would be allowed to join the Yonsei team for the 2003 fall semester despite still being a high school senior.{{cite news|title=농구대잔치-최장신 하승진, 5경기만에 `이름값`|url=https://news.kbs.co.kr/news/view.do?ncd=1060815|publisher=[[Korean Broadcasting System|KBS]]|date=25 November 2003|language=ko}} His contemporaries at Yonsei included Yang and future [[Jeonju KCC Egis]] teammate [[Kim Tae-sul]]. After playing only seven games for Yonsei, he left for the United States to make himself eligible for the [[2004 NBA draft]].The academic year in South Korea begins in February.{{cite news|title=하승진, 한국인 최초 NBA 입성|url=https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/354506#home|work=[[JoongAng Ilbo]]|date=25 June 2004|language=ko}} ==Professional career== ===NBA career (2004–2007)=== Ha arrived in [[Los Angeles, California]] in 2004 to prepare himself for the [[2004 NBA draft]]. Ha was drafted with the 46th overall selection by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He played briefly with the [[Portland Reign]] of the [[American Basketball Association (21st century)|ABA]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ha_seung-jin/bio.html |title=Ha Seung-Jin info page |work=NBA.com |date=1985-08-04 |access-date=2012-08-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616124209/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ha_seung-jin/bio.html |archive-date=2012-06-16 }} Ha joined the Portland Trail Blazers in the middle of the [[2004-05 NBA season|2004-05 season]]. Ha played in only 19 games that season, averaging 5.5 minutes per game; however, on April 20 against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], he scored a career high 13 points to help the Trail Blazers win the game. During the [[2005-06 NBA season|2005-06 season]] Ha was assigned to the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]'s [[Fort Worth Flyers]] on March 28, 2006,{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_05-06.html |title=2005-06 Transactions |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-08-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070112095435/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_05-06.html |archive-date=2007-01-12 }} where he played for five games but did not make an impact. When fellow Blazer centers [[Theo Ratliff]] and [[Joel Przybilla]] were unable to play due to injury, Ha started four games, averaging 11 minutes playing time. On July 31, 2006, Ha was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a four-player deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Jamaal_Magliore-185803-1218.html |title=BLAZERS: Trail Blazers Acquire All-Star Center Jamaal Magloire |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-08-03}} On October 28, 2006 (prior to the start of the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006-07 season]]{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070207.html |title=Bucks, D-League Building Productive Pipeline |work=Nba.com |date=2007-02-07 |access-date=2012-08-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080316004818/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070207.html |archive-date=2008-03-16 |url-status=dead }}), he was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=buckshaseungjin&prov=st&type=lgns |title=Bucks waive Korean Ha Seung-Jin |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date=2006-10-28 |access-date=2012-08-03 |archive-date=2007-03-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312095749/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=buckshaseungjin&prov=st&type=lgns |url-status=dead }} He was acquired by the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on December 31, 2006,{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |title=2006-07 Transactions |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-08-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618011602/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |archive-date=2015-06-18 |url-status=dead }} whom he spent time with. ===Jeonju KCC Egis (2008–2019)=== Ha returned to South Korea and joined the 2008 [[Korean Basketball League]] draft, signing with [[Jeonju KCC Egis]]. He won the 2009 and 2011 KBL Championships, winning the play-off MVP award in the latter. After the 2018–19 season ended, he became a free agent and chose to retire rather than re-sign or join another team.{{cite news|title=하승진, 은퇴 선언 글에 시선집중…"말도 잘하는데 글도 ==Post-retirement== In 2020, Ha became a commentator for the [[Korean Broadcasting System]]'s sports channel [[KBS N|KBS N Sports]] and mainly commentates for [[Women's Korean Basketball League]] (WKBL) games.{{cite news|title=[영상] 초대형 해설이 온다! 221cm 하승진 KBS에서 해설 데뷔|url=https://news.kbs.co.kr/news/view.do?ncd=5021843|publisher=[[Korean Broadcasting System|KBS]]|date=9 October 2020|language=ko}} He was a guest commentator for basketball events at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]].{{cite news|title=박찬호·조원희→여홍철·하승진, 金 쏘아 올릴 KBS 도쿄올림픽 해설진|url=https://www.chosun.com/entertainments/entertain_photo/2021/07/21/LZ7QOQV3YU434OYJ3VMEF7FLUQ/|work=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]|date=21 July 2021|language=ko}} ==Personal life== Ha is the younger of two children. His older sister, {{ill|Ha Eun-joo|ko|하은주}}, was also a professional basketball player. A 6'8" center, she signed with the [[Los Angeles Sparks]] of the [[WNBA]] on February 6, 2006,{{cite web|url=http://www.wnba.com/sparks/news/ha_signs_060207.html |title=Sparks Sign Korean Center Ha Eun-Joo |publisher=Wnba.com |access-date=2012-08-03}} and was later waived on May 19, for failing to arrive in Los Angeles. She hadn’t arrived because of a conflicting contract with [[Chanson V-Magic]] of the [[Women's Japan Basketball League|WJBL]].{{cite web |author=Contact rickchand: Comment |url=http://www.deadspin.com/sports/nba/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-milwaukee-bucks-205116.php |title=Five Tiny Tidbits On: The Milwaukee Bucks |publisher=Deadspin.com |date=2006-10-04 |access-date=2012-08-03 |archive-date=September 26, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926233900/http://www.deadspin.com/sports/nba/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-milwaukee-bucks-205116.php |url-status=dead }} In July 2006, she signed with [[Incheon Shinhan Bank S-Birds]] of the [[Women's Korean Basketball League|WKBL]]. Their father Ha Dong-gi is a former basketball player-turned-coach who played for [[Myongji University]] but who gave up the sport due to chronic injury problems. Ha Dong-gi had been a member of the [[Basketball at the 1978 Asian Games|team]] which won silver at the [[1978 Asian Games]]. Ha married Kim Hwa-yeong in 2012.{{cite news|title=‘아내의 맛’ 하승진♥ 아내, 자다 깬 얼굴도_결혼 8년차 주부의 미모|url=https://sports.donga.com/ent/article/all/20191106/98234170/1|work=[[The Dong-a Ilbo]]|date=6 November 2019|language=ko}}{{cite news|title=하승진 "권나라는 비주얼 1티어다"…아내 등장에 그가 취한 행동은?|url=http://woman.chosun.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=76278|work=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]|date=5 May 2021|language=ko}} They have a son (born in 2012) and a daughter (born in 2017).{{cite news|title=하승진, "딸에게 좌절과 실패 알려주려고.." 딸 손잡고 태권도장 등록!|url=https://news.jtbc.joins.com/article/article.aspx?news_id=NB12001726|publisher=[[JTBC]]|date=25 April 2021|language=ko}} == Filmography == === Television show === {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" |- ! scope="col" | Year ! scope="col" | Title ! scope="col" | Role ! scope="col" class="unsortable" | {{abbr|Ref.|Reference(s)}} |- ! scope="row"| 2022 | ''Over the Top'' | Contestant |{{cite web|url=https://entertain.naver.com/now/read?oid=052&aid=0001794995|author=Oh Ji-won|title=팔씨름 예능 '오버더톱' 10월 첫 방송…전현무→하승진 출연|trans-title=Arm wrestling entertainment 'Over the Top' premieres in October...
